Basic Information for CVE-2026-42042 Vulnerability Information Axios: XSRF Token Cross-Origin Leakage via Prototype Pollution Gadget in withXSRFToken Boolean Coercion Overview In versions of Axios prior to 1.15.1 (browser-side) and 0.31.1 (Node.js-side), the withXSRFToken configuration option is evaluated using JavaScript’s truthy/falsy semantics instead of strict boolean comparison. This causes the same-origin check to be skipped when the value is a truthy non-boolean type, resulting in the XSRF token being sent to any request target—including attacker-controlled cross-origin servers. Affected Versions Axios < 1.15.1 (browser-side) Axios < 0.31.1 (Node.js-side) Details The XSRF protection logic relies on withXSRFToken to determine whether to attach the token. The code uses truthy/falsy semantics for this configuration, rather than strict === true/false. When withXSRFToken is set to any truthy non-boolean type (e.g., via prototype pollution or misconfiguration), the same-origin check (isURLSameOrigin) is short-circuited. Result: The XSRF token is sent with requests to all targets, including cross-origin servers controlled by an attacker. Impact An attacker can induce the client to send requests containing the XSRF token to a malicious cross-origin server, bypassing same-origin restrictions, which may lead to successful cross-site request forgery attacks.
